FTQ-001.evidence: In crates/sc-agent-http/tests/ureq.rs, test_timeout_is_network_error_without_the_key (line 203) now builds Timeouts::new(2 s connect, 1 s request). The old value was 150 ms. A code comment says the stall is the only possible cause. The stall server is unchanged in behavior: Reply::Stall waits on released.recv_timeout(SERVER_DEADLINE) in tests/support/mod.rs:249-251. A longer client timeout cannot make the test pass for the wrong reason, so this is not masking. No retry, sleep or compensating branch was added. The remaining assertions are unchanged: kind is Timeout, retryable, no key leak, and server.finish().len() == 1.

fix_round_regression_check.renamed_connect_test: test_connect_phase_failure_is_retryable_and_not_retried accepts Connect or Timeout. This is a platform-behavior accommodation (Windows retries the SYN). The wait is bounded by the 2 s connect timeout, and the test still asserts retryable and exactly one send. I did not treat it as masking.
fix_round_regression_check.bounded_waits: The LoopbackServer support code is bounded throughout. finish() uses done.recv_timeout(FINISH_DEADLINE) and panics with a clear message. Accepted streams get read and write timeouts. The stall wait uses recv_timeout. The accept loop checks the shutdown flag and the start time.
fix_round_regression_check.residual_note_not_a_finding: refused_port() binds an ephemeral port and drops it. In theory another concurrently running loopback test could be handed that port. This is a very low-probability, pre-existing pattern that the fix round did not introduce. Under the locked-round rules I am not reporting it.
